Reconstruct mutual-rank values for a gene subset

Source: R/mr_block.R
mr_block.Rd

Computes the exact mutual rank values for a subset of genes. Uses the stored parameters of the network (cor_method, sign, mr_log_transform). Recovers values that a sparse network discards.

Usage

mr_block(x, genes, net)

Arguments

x

Expression matrix (genes x samples) the network was built from. Must contain every network gene as a row; extra rows (e.g. genes removed as constant) are ignored.

genes

Character vector of gene identifiers (no duplicates), all present in rownames(net$network).

net

Network object from compute_network() (sparse or dense) with norm_method = "MR".

Value

A k x k numeric matrix of mutual-rank values with dimnames = list(genes, genes) and zero diagonal, on the same scale as the network (raw MR, or log-normalized when the network was built with mr_log_transform = TRUE).

Details

A sparse network (compute_network(sparse = TRUE)) discards values below its store_threshold. This function reconstructs them, for example for a module heatmap, without rebuilding the dense n x n matrix. The value \(MR_{ij} = \sqrt{R_{ij} R_{ji}}\) only needs the correlations of genes i and j ranked over all n network genes, so a k x n correlation slice suffices.

The gene universe is rownames(net$network): x is subset to those rows first (the constant-gene filter was already applied when the network was built), and ranks span exactly the network genes. Pass the same expression matrix that built the network; the reconstructed block then matches the dense compute_network(sparse = FALSE) matrix.

Reconstruction is exact up to ties in the correlation values: exactly tied correlations get average ranks, and a mathematical tie can be broken differently by this function (stats::cor()) and the network's correlation backend (Rfast::cora()), shifting a rank by 0.5. Ties are measure-zero for Pearson on continuous data, but Spearman correlations lie on a finite grid where occasional ties are possible.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
net <- compute_network(x, density = 0.03) # sparse
# exact values for one module, including sub-threshold entries:
blk <- mr_block(x, module_genes, net)
heatmap(blk)
} # }
